projects.title: Ideal customer profile, 30 target accounts and a 3-week outbound sequence
projects.summary: Choose a real B2B company and its product (public information only), define its ideal customer profile and buyer personas, build a list of 30 target accounts with a reason to contact each one now, and write a 3-week multichannel sequence (e-mails, call script, LinkedIn) with the metrics you would track.
projects.why: Prospecting is the first job of an SDR and a large part of an Account Executive’s week. A targeted account list and a sequence written for real buyers show recruiters that you can fill a pipeline on day one, not only talk about it.

data.name: HubSpot Academy: free sales courses
data.note: Free courses on prospecting, sales e-mails and inbound sales, with certificates.

data.name: HubSpot free CRM
data.note: A free CRM to store your accounts and contacts and run the sequence.

data.name: Salesforce Trailhead
data.note: Free Salesforce training: the CRM most B2B sales teams use.

steps.title: Choose the company and the product
steps.text: Pick a real B2B company whose product you can understand from its website (a SaaS tool, a logistics service, an industrial supplier). Write in a few lines what it sells, to whom, the problem it solves and its price level if public.

steps.title: Define the ideal customer profile
steps.text: Describe the companies that get the most value: sector, size, country (France or Europe), tools they use, signs of need. Add two or three buyer personas (for example Head of Sales, Operations Director) with their goals, pains and objections.

steps.title: Build the list of 30 accounts
steps.text: Find 30 real companies that match the profile, from public sources (websites, news, job ads, LinkedIn company pages). For each one: name, size, why it fits, the persona to contact (role, not personal data) and a trigger that makes now a good time.

steps.title: Write the sequence
steps.text: Write a 3-week sequence of 8 to 10 steps: 4 short e-mails (each with one idea and one question), 3 calls with a 30-second opening script and answers to two objections, and 2 LinkedIn steps (connection, then a useful message). Show where you personalise with the trigger.

steps.title: Set it up in a CRM
steps.text: Create a few of the accounts in a free CRM, with fictional contacts, the sequence steps as tasks and the pipeline stages (new, contacted, replied, meeting booked, qualified).

steps.title: Define the metrics
steps.text: Write the targets you would track each week: open rate, reply rate, positive replies, meetings booked, meetings that become qualified opportunities, and what you would change if a number is too low.

steps.title: Present it
steps.text: Make a short deck or one-page document: the profile, the top 10 accounts with their trigger, the sequence and the metrics.

deliverables: The ideal customer profile and two or three buyer personas
The list of 30 target accounts (sheet) with fit, persona and trigger
The 3-week sequence: e-mails, call script and LinkedIn messages
A metrics table with targets and what to do when a number is low
checklist: Every account on the list has a written reason to fit the profile
At least 10 accounts have a recent, specific trigger
E-mails are short (under 120 words) and end with one question
The call script has an opening, two discovery questions and answers to two objections
The metrics go as far as qualified opportunities, not only replies
No personal data of real people is published: roles only, contacts in the CRM are fictional

cv.bullet: Designed a B2B outbound campaign for [company] (personal project): ideal customer profile, 30 researched target accounts, a 3-week multichannel sequence (e-mail, phone, LinkedIn) set up in HubSpot CRM and a weekly metrics plan.
cv.talk: Explain how you chose the profile, the trigger you liked most on your list, and what you would change if the reply rate stayed under 3 %.

stretch: Send the sequence to 10 people you know who match a persona and ask for honest feedback.
Write a second version of the first e-mail and explain how you would A/B test it.
Get the HubSpot Academy inbound sales certificate and add it to your CV.

projects.title: CRM pipeline analysis: win rates, sales cycle and next quarter’s forecast
projects.summary: Analyse a real-format CRM opportunities dataset: win rate by stage, product and sales agent, length of the sales cycle and deal size, then build a forecast for next quarter and recommend three actions to the sales manager, in Excel or Power BI.
projects.why: Sales managers judge salespeople on how well they know their numbers. A clear pipeline analysis with a forecast shows that you can read a CRM like a manager, a strong point for an SDR moving to Account Executive or for a sales operations role.

data.name: Maven Analytics Data Playground
data.note: Free datasets: take “CRM Sales Opportunities” (B2B opportunities with stages, products, agents and dates).

data.name: Kaggle Learn: Pandas
data.note: A free short course if you prefer to do the analysis in Python.

steps.title: Understand the data
steps.text: Download the dataset, read its data dictionary and list the tables (opportunities, accounts, products, sales teams). Write what one row means and which columns give the stage, the dates and the amount.

steps.title: Clean and join
steps.text: Join the tables, check missing values and inconsistent names, and add columns: deal duration in days (close date minus engage date), quarter, won or lost.

steps.title: Measure the win rate
steps.text: Compute the win rate on closed deals overall, then by product, by sales agent, by manager and by account sector. Note the gaps that are large enough to matter.

steps.title: Measure cycle and deal size
steps.text: Compute the average and median sales cycle and deal size for won deals, by product. Check whether long deals are won less often.

steps.title: Look at the open pipeline
steps.text: For the deals still open, show the value by stage and by agent, and the deals that have been open much longer than the usual cycle.

steps.title: Forecast next quarter
steps.text: Build a simple forecast: open pipeline value by stage × the historical win rate of that stage, plus the usual new business. Show a low, expected and high figure and write your assumptions.

steps.title: Recommend three actions
steps.text: Make a dashboard and a one-page note for the sales manager: the three main findings and three concrete actions (for example coaching on one product, cleaning stale deals, focusing on a sector).

deliverables: The cleaned dataset or Power BI model with the added columns
A dashboard: win rate, cycle length, deal size and open pipeline by stage, product and agent
A next-quarter forecast with assumptions and a low / expected / high range
A one-page note to the sales manager with three actions
checklist: Win rates are computed on closed deals only (won ÷ (won + lost))
The sales cycle uses won deals and shows the median, not only the average
Every comparison between agents or products gives the number of deals behind it
The forecast states its assumptions and gives a range
Each action is tied to a finding and to a number

cv.bullet: Analysed a B2B CRM pipeline of [n] opportunities (personal project): win rate by stage, product and agent, sales cycle and deal size, a next-quarter forecast and three recommendations, in Power BI.
cv.talk: Explain the finding that surprised you most, how you built the forecast and its main assumption, and which action you would start with.

stretch: Add a weighted pipeline coverage ratio against a quarterly target you define.
Compare your stage-based forecast with a simple trend on past quarters.
Redo the analysis in Python with pandas and compare the effort.

projects.title: Key account plan for a listed company, with a MEDDIC qualification and a mock discovery call
projects.summary: Choose a product you could sell and a real listed company as the target customer. Use its annual report to find its priorities, map the likely buying committee, qualify the opportunity with MEDDIC, write a 90-day account plan and record a mock discovery call.
projects.why: Account Executives and Key Account Managers are hired on how they handle large, complex accounts. An account plan built from the client’s own annual report, with a real qualification and a recorded call, shows the preparation and the discovery skills that interviews test.

data.name: SEC EDGAR full-text search
data.note: Annual reports (10-K) of US-listed companies: strategy, risks and figures, free.

data.name: HubSpot Academy: free sales courses
data.note: Free courses on discovery calls, sales methods and account management.

steps.title: Choose the product and the account
steps.text: Pick a product you understand (a real B2B product or the one from your outbound project) and a large listed company that could buy it. Explain in a few lines why this account is a good fit.

steps.title: Read the annual report
steps.text: From the annual report (10-K, or the universal registration document of a French company), note the strategy, three business priorities, the main risks and key figures (revenue, growth, headcount). Link each priority to something your product can help with.

steps.title: Map the buying committee
steps.text: List the roles that would be involved in the decision: economic buyer, users, technical evaluator, purchasing, legal, and a possible champion. For each role: what they care about and the likely objection. Use roles and public titles only.

steps.title: Qualify with MEDDIC
steps.text: Fill in Metrics, Economic buyer, Decision criteria, Decision process, Identify pain and Champion with what you know from public sources and what you would need to find out. Give the deal an honest status.

steps.title: Write the 90-day plan
steps.text: Plan the first 90 days: who to contact first and how, the meetings to get, the value proposition per persona, the proof (case study, pilot) and the milestones with dates and an estimated deal value.

steps.title: Prepare the discovery call
steps.text: Write a call plan: the goal of the call, a short opening, 10 open discovery questions about their situation, pain, impact and decision process, and the next step you will ask for.

steps.title: Record a mock call
steps.text: Record a 15-minute mock discovery call with a friend playing the buyer. Listen to it, count how long each side talks, and write what you would change.

deliverables: An account plan (deck of 8 to 10 slides): priorities, buying committee, MEDDIC, 90-day plan
The discovery call plan with the questions
The recording of the mock call (or its transcript) and a short self-review
checklist: Each business priority quotes the annual report and its page or section
The buying committee names roles, their interests and their likely objections
MEDDIC separates what is known from what still has to be found out
The 90-day plan has dated milestones and a next step for each
In the mock call, the buyer talks more than you do
No confidential or personal information is used: public sources and roles only

cv.bullet: Built a key account plan for [company] (personal project): priorities from its annual report, buying committee map, MEDDIC qualification, 90-day plan and a recorded mock discovery call.
cv.talk: Explain which priority from the annual report you would open with, who you think the economic buyer is and why, and what the mock call taught you.

stretch: Write the mutual action plan you would propose to the client after a successful first meeting.
Build a simple business case (cost of the problem vs price of the solution) with figures from the annual report.
Redo the plan for a competitor of the same company and compare the two accounts.
